card.name: Treating non-humans as people
card.fires_on: Small words in passages where something non-human (an institution, an animal, fortune, the universe) is described as if it were a person, just before a word like anthropomorphic or personified would fit.

modes.label: Personifying wording
modes.description: Linking words inside phrases that give human traits or agency to abstract things, such as 'conceived as having' or 'endowed with a spirit'.
modes.example: Cyclopedia - n. Fortune; hap; that which happens to a person by chance, conceived as<< having>> a real tendency to be favorable or unfavorable

modes.label: Animals given human traits
modes.description: Verbs in descriptions of cartoons or stories where an animal is given clothes or human behavior.
modes.example: created by Tagawa Suiho in 1931, in which the cartoonist<< gives>> an octopus clothes and shoes to fit

card.writes: It pushes toward words like anthropomorphic, person and personification, and away from unrelated religious words.
card.plain: It notices when a text is treating a thing or animal as if it were a person.
